newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gold - Price fall seen lifting S.E.Asian demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gold - Price fall seen lifting S.E.Asian demand.

text.p: The slide in world gold prices to 12-year lows following the Australian central bank's sale of 167 tonnes of gold held in its reserves, is expected to lift physical demand in Southeast Asia, dealers said on Friday.
"The news will trigger more interest in the physical side. Generally we will see good speculator buying," one said.
But dealers said it was still too early to get a clear view of price trends and buyers may wait for the dust to settle from gold's overnight plunge before entering the market.
One dealer said he expected the bear trend to continue until September/October.
Around the region, dealers expected the price slump to trigger fair demand in Indonesia, but they still doubted it would match the offtake in January/February due to a seasonal lull in purchasing.

Gold buying in Thailand has been robust this week, but dealers said this was linked largely to the flotation of the baht which sparked a 20 percent drop in the Thai currency and a knee-jerk flight of capital into investment safe havens.
